condition: suspected acute ascending inflammatory demyelinating syndrome presenting with progressive bilateral lower-limb weakness ascending to the thighs over 2 days 2 weeks after acute diarrhea
level_rationale: Rapidly progressive weakness in both legs climbing up to the thighs over 2 days occurring 2 weeks after an acute diarrheal illness in a 34-year-old adult raises urgent suspicion for acute ascending inflammatory demyelinating neuropathy with imminent risk of bulbar dysfunction and neuromuscular respiratory failure requiring immediate emergency department neurological evaluation, spirometry, lumbar puncture, and immunotherapy readiness, whereas having felt mild tiredness in the legs for 1 hour on the day that diarrhea ended 2 weeks ago reflects resolved transient post-diarrheal fatigue requiring no medical care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + uncontracted causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A post-diarrheal resolved brief leg tiredness self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 34, acute diarrhea 2 weeks ago, and worsening weakness in both legs climbing to the thighs over 2 days) with zero apostrophe contractions, explicit first-person subject agreement ('Im 34 and had ... and I have had ... over 2 days'), a 2-word span difference (7 vs 9 words), and zero banned diagnosis words ('guillain' and 'polyneuropathy' omitted). Anchoring the Rule A control ('felt mild tiredness in my legs for 1 hour the day that diarrhea ended') directly to f2 keeps 'in my legs' identical, adds zero unstated exercise triggers, and shifts right care cleanly from ER (level 4) to self-care (level 1) with zero stated negatives.
